hints.title: Two Zigzag Parity Patterns
hints.text: A zigzag sequence either has every even index strictly smaller than its neighbors, or every odd index strictly smaller than its neighbors.

hints.title: Independent Cost Evaluation
hints.text: Decreasing only valley elements guarantees that peak elements never need modification, keeping operations independent.

hints.title: Target Element Valley Condition
hints.text: For chosen valley index i, decrease it so that nums[i] is at most min(left_neighbor, right_neighbor) - 1. Compute costs for both parities and return the minimum.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Modifying peak elements complicates adjacent comparisons, whereas decreasing valleys preserves local independence.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Evaluating both even-valley and odd-valley choices in a single linear pass uses zero extra storage.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize that only valley elements need to be decreased, separating the problem into parity 0 vs parity 1.
complexity.notes: Out-of-bounds neighbors are treated as positive infinity.
